subject: Post-call: BlueVale trial & technical integration plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@bluevale.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BlueVale trial & technical integration plan

Hi Sara / Max —

Thanks again for the time today. Wildly productive call — I wanted to capture the call recap, proposed success criteria for the 4-week trial, and a minimal technical integration plan so we all have the same starting point. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Call recap (2/3 bullets):
- Use case: semantic search + extractive QA over BlueVale's internal research corpus; initial scope ~200k docs (PDFs + HTML).
- Desired UX: sub-250ms first-token latency for a 512-token generate path when using streaming; embeddings for recall with batch upsert.
- Constraints: data residency in us-east-1, SOC2 evidence requested, and a commercial SLT for latency for demo audiences.

Proposed 4-week trial (high level):
1) Success criteria (measureable):
   - Retrieval + generate pipeline achieves MRR@10 improvement >= 9% on the 200 test queries we agreed on (you'll provide baseline).
   - Median first-token latency <250ms for the streaming generate API at target qps (10 qps simulated).
   - Embedding cosine recall (top-5) >= baseline + 6%.
   - No PII leakage incidents; Redwood to provide audit trace for all requests.
2) Timeline:
   - Week 0 (this week): kickoff + infra access + SSO invite + shared PoC doc.
   - Week 1: SDK integration (ingest + embedding batch upsert), initial embedding quality checks.
   - Week 2: Retrieval + generate integration, enable streaming and tool-calling for external KB lookups.
   - Week 3: Load/run test harness, iterate models/quantization suggestions.
   - Week 4: Acceptance window and demo to stakeholders.
3) Ownership:
   - BlueVale: Sara (product lead), Max (infra).
   - Redwood: Vivek (sales), Grace (solutions eng - technical lead), Rachel (on-call infra contact).

Technical integration highlights (minimal):
- Use Redwood JS SDK (v2.1.0) for embeddings and streaming generation.
- API routes: POST /v1/embeddings (batch upsert), POST /v1/generate for non-streaming, POST /v1/stream for chunked streaming responses.
- Tool calling: use Redwood's functions schema to attach knowledge-base lookups; we recommend implementing a lookup tool that calls your internal KB API with a key-scoped service account.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts; Redwood will provide suggested cache keys and TTLs after initial run.

Attachments: I attached a concise success-matrix and a recommended PoC architecture diagram.

Next steps (owners + dates):
- Sara: share 200 test queries + baseline metrics by Mon 11/02.
- Max: provide service account + minimal ingress IP allowlist by Wed 11/04.
- Grace: create integration checklist and sample code snippets by Mon 11/02.
- Vivek: schedule kickoff (15–30 min) for Tue 11/03; create shared doc and HubSpot deal entry.

If all that sounds good I'll schedule the kickoff and loop in infra for the SSO+service account.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical notes and a proposed minimal-implementation checklist. Quoting Vivek below for context.

On Sat, Oct 31, 2026 at 3:22 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Technical integration highlights (minimal):
> - Use Redwood JS SDK (v2.1.0) for embeddings and streaming generation.
> - API routes: POST /v1/embeddings (batch upsert), POST /v1/generate for non-streaming, POST /v1/stream for chunked streaming responses.

Confirmed: SDK will be the fastest path. A few specifics for the engineering team to implement this week: 
- SDK: use redwood-js@2.1.0, example: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-east-1' });
- Embeddings: batch upsert via POST /v1/embeddings with content_id + metadata. Aim for bulk sizes of 500 docs per request to avoid timeouts; we'll provide retry guidance.
- Streaming: streaming uses Server-Sent Events (chunked) over /v1/stream. Example curl (pseudo):
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-lite-2","prompt":"..."}'
  Read chunks and assemble tokens.
- Tool calling: Redwood follows the function-calling contract; we suggest implementing a single "kb_lookup" tool that returns JSON in the function response. We'll include a TypeScript example in the checklist.
- Observability: enable debug level request logging for the first 48 hours; Redwood console will provide per-route latency breakdowns and token cost.

Minimal implementation checklist (for week 1):
1) Create RW service account & API key (BlueVale).
2) Install redwood-js client and run the embedding batch upsert for a 1k doc sample.
3) Wire up streaming generate path with a simple page to test first-token times.
4) Implement tool-calling shim to your KB API and validate JSON responses.
5) Provide sample traces/logs to Redwood (Rachel) for the 2nd-week load testing.

I'll drop the checklist and sample code snippets into the shared doc now. Rachel — please hold on the load-test infra CIDRs until Max shares your allowlist.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai
